substantive_checks.arbitrary_sum_divisor: PASS: prime-by-prime valuations prove gcd(Q,R)/gcd(Q,B) divides R/B for every finite nonzero integer sum, with no sparsity or degree restriction
substantive_checks.conditional_height_ceiling: PASS: the explicit normalized l1-height hypothesis log(sum |T_j|/B)=O(n) gives only an O(n)=o(n log n) additive quotient; it is not asserted for arbitrary unbounded constructions without that hypothesis
substantive_checks.reservoir_deoverlap: PASS: targets are declared inside q_n/gcd(q_n,D_m), and gcd(Q,B) is retained as the unresolved Item282 common-product baseline rather than rebooked
substantive_checks.boundary_unit_reduction: PASS: C_h is congruent to -P_h(n)q_(n+1)^2 modulo q_n, so unequal Casoratian degrees give the exact residual F(u) with u=-q_(n+1)^2, and the prefactor is a Q-unit
substantive_checks.small_lift_criterion: PASS: a factorization-independent unit lift with O(n) normalized evaluated height closes only the additive quotient; the canonical lift costs at least 2 log q_(n+1)=2n log n+O(n) for a genuinely nonhomogeneous sum
substantive_checks.homogenization_scope: PASS: multiplication by powers of C_1 creates a different designed homogeneous scalar controlled by F(1); no implication from the original F(u) collision is claimed
substantive_checks.resultant_criterion: PASS: a monic integer annihilator M(u)=0 modulo Q and the Sylvester-Bezout identity give prime-power divisibility of the additive quotient into Res(M,F/B); nonzero O(n)-height is an explicit conditional requirement
substantive_checks.zero_resultant_scope: PASS: a zero resultant is explicitly left open and is not used as a height certificate
substantive_checks.target_independence: PASS: the report excludes constructions chosen from the target factorization or unknown p-adic depths; the bounded checker is labeled exact finite only
substantive_checks.capacity_booking: PASS: neither a low-height actual-family lift/annihilator nor the product-return theorem is proved, so the Route-1 rate and beta-capacity reduction are both booked as zero

strict_scope.proved: Arbitrary finite sums have a universal normalized cancellation divisor; actual nonhomogeneous Casoratian sums reduce exactly to a boundary-unit polynomial and admit conditional low-height lift or annihilator-resultant closures.
strict_scope.finite_only: Checker examples verify exact identities, non-transfer witnesses, and resultant behavior but imply no asymptotic distribution theorem.
strict_scope.open: A factorization-independent O(n)-height lift or nonzero annihilator resultant for the actual unit, the Item282 product baseline, the beta weighted-return theorem, and all positive-rate consequences remain open.
